correctness.rationale: With S1=S2=[-1,1], U1=-x²/2+xy and U2=-(1-b)y²/2+(x-x³)y, the own-strategy second derivatives are -1 and -(1-b)<0 throughout 0≤b≤1/2. Best response 1 is x=y; |x-x³|≤2/(3sqrt3) and denominator 1-b≥1/2 ensure player 2 best response y=(x-x³)/(1-b) is always strictly interior. Equilibrium thus reduces without missing boundary equilibria to x(x²-b)=0: unique (0,0) at b0 and 3 equilibria (±sqrt b,±sqrt b),(0,0) for any b>0. Joint first-order derivative matrix [[-1,1],[1,-1]] has determinant zero at b0; own concavity does not imply joint nonsingularity. This directly contradicts the printed local-unique structural stability conclusion under its own hypotheses, but not the separate existence/accumulation results.

final_claim: An admissible two-player singleton-type instance of the 2026 Bayesian utility-perturbation model has strictly concave twice differentiable own-action utilities for all b in [0,1/2] but exactly one Nash/Bayesian equilibrium at b=0 and exactly three for every b>0, contradicting the source Theorem 3 and its Corollary 1 about local equilibrium uniqueness/stability.
limitations: Local non-uniqueness refutes Theorem 3 and dependent Corollary 1; no assertion about stronger repaired theorem or general equilibrium persistence.
